grammar_focus: KS20+KS44 动名词 -ing 作动词宾语(avoid/enjoy/deny/finish/mind + doing;It's no use/not worth doing、be busy doing、prevent sb from doing)(教材 L68 Key structures)主考;动名词的逻辑主语(mind my doing)、感官动词 see/hear/smell + doing、go/come + doing、反义疑问句(辅考)
scene: 我穿过马路想躲开他,可他看见我,挥了挥手。装作没看见他也没用,于是我也挥手回应。我从来不喜欢碰见奈杰尔·戴克斯——他总是闲得没事干。不管你多忙,他总是坚持要跟着一起。我得想个办法,别让他跟着我逛一上午。“真巧在这儿碰到你!”他说,“你没忙什么吧?”“你介意我跟你一起去吗?”我还没说完他就问。我得赶紧想辙。“完全不介意,”我说,“不过我要去看牙医。”我以为这能让他打退堂鼓,可我错了。“那我也去,”他说,“候诊室里总有一堆东西可以读!”

grammar_card.title: 动名词 -ing 作动词宾语
grammar_card.intro: KS20+KS44 有些动词/结构后面只能接动名词(-ing),不接不定式:①动词 avoid/enjoy/deny/finish/mind/keep + doing;②结构 It's no use doing(做…没用)、It's not worth doing(不值得做)、be busy doing(忙于做)、prevent sb from doing(阻止某人做)。另:动名词可带逻辑主语(mind my coming);感官动词 see/hear/smell + 人/物 + doing;go/come + doing(go dancing)。

rows: I avoid meeting him. / He enjoys playing football.
It's no use / not worth doing
It's no use crying about it.
I prevented him from following me.
I saw him coming. / go dancing

specialRules.rule: 动名词可带逻辑主语,用物主代词:Would you mind opening…?(泛指)转成 Would you mind my opening…?(强调是“我”开);Fancy her writing a letter like that!
反义疑问句前后相反:陈述肯定→疑问否定;陈述否定→疑问肯定。You're not busy, are you?(前否后肯)/ He insists on coming, doesn't he?(前肯后否)。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Why did Elizabeth tell Nigel that she was going to the dentist?
options: To stop Nigel from following her around all morning
Because she really had a toothache
Because Nigel worked at the dentist's
Because she wanted him to come with her

passage: I crossed the street to avoid meeting him, but he saw me and waved. It was no use pretending I hadn't seen him, so I waved back. I never enjoy meeting Nigel Dykes — he never has anything to do. No matter how busy you are, he always insists on coming along. I had to think of a way of preventing him from following me around all morning. 'Fancy meeting you here!' he said. 'You're not busy doing anything, are you?' 'Would you mind my coming with you?' he asked before I could finish. I had to think fast. 'Not at all,' I said, 'but I'm going to the dentist.' I thought that would stop him, but I was wrong. 'Then I'll come too,' he said. 'There's always plenty to read in the waiting room!'
